To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the quadratic Renyi and log-energy entropy-based measures computed in the ensemble empirical decomposition (EEM) domain are more promising in discriminating between the focal and nonfocal electroencephlography (EEG) signal than the other entropy-based features.
the entropy-based features are more promising in discriminating focal and non-focalelectroencephalography signals in EEMD domain.
the quadratic Renyi and log-energy entropy features are most promising in distinguishing the focal and non focal EEG signals in EEMD domain.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an effective and reliable technique to discriminate between focal and non-focals signals.
the development and analysis of entropy-based measures for the discrimination of focal and nonfocal EEG signals in the EEMDM and CEEMDAM domains.
the analysis of the EEG signals in the EEMDM and CEEMD domains.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the entropy-based measures computed in the CEEMDAN and EEMD domains are more effective in discriminating the non-focal and focal EEG signals.
the quadratic Renyi and log-energy entropy-based features computed from the differences of EEG signals are most promising in distinguishing the focal and nonfocal EEG signals.
the entropy-based measures computed in the CEEMDAN are better than those computed in the EMD.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the entropy-based features calculated in the EMD domain are useful in the discrimination of the EEG signals and the quadratic Renyi and log-energy entropy features are the best among all entropy measures.
the entropy-based features computed in the EMD domains of the EEG signals can effectively discriminate the focal and non focal EEG signals.
the quadratic Renyi and log-energy entropy-based features are more promising in the discrimination of the EEG signals from the EEMD domain than from the CEEMDAN.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the entropy measures computed on the EEMD or CEEMDAN decomposed EEG signals can be used to discriminate the focal and nonfocal EEG signals.
the entropy-based features calculated in the EMD domains are more effective in discriminating focal and non-focals than in the time domain.
the entropy-based measures in the EEMDs and CEEMDAn domains are promising to discriminate the focal and nonfocal EEG signals.
